newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends modestly higher as crude teeters.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends modestly higher as crude teeters.

text.p: IPE May gas oil closed $1.75 higher at $170.75 on Friday but some traders said the rise was largely due to pre-weekend position squaring mixed with some fundamentals.
June gas oil also closed unchanged at $167.50. The May contract had hit a high of $171.25 but also a low of $169.00.
"It's just manipulation. June got sold and May got bid up. The market has been very well offered all afternoon," one broker said.
"There are fundamentals (behind the rise), the market is a little bit stronger obviously with the Singapore market being stronger and products strong in the (United) States.
"But if you look at the crack, gas oil is not strong. The crack has come of 20 points, it's hardly strong," he added.
Other traders said the market was drawing strength from forecasts of colder weather in the Northeast United States for the weekend.

June Brent, which hit a session high of $18.87, was trading five cents higher at $18.74 a barrel at 1712 GMT. The contract shed all of its earlier gains and dipped to about $18.63 aftr NYMEX slipped but it recovered later.
